front.title: An Agentic AI Framework for Hallucination Mitigation in Network Intent Translation

author.organization: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Department of Computer Science and Engineering
Department of Computer Science and Engineering

abstract.t: This document describes an agentic AI workflow for detecting and mitigating structural and semantic errors, including hallucinated policy content, when translating a natural-language network intent into structured policies. The workflow coordinates role-specialized language-model functions with deterministic validation tools within a predefined action space and a bounded retry budget. Schema- constrained generation limits structural defects, while cross-slot checks and intent-faithfulness assessment identify a potentially unsupported or inconsistent policy content. Structured validation traces guide targeted re-extraction and regeneration. Unresolved cases retain explicit failure status for downstream review. This document describes component interactions, validation outcomes, and recovery behavior, and also presents a 3GPP TS 28.312-based instantiation for mobile network management.
